newsitem.title: BELGIUM: No new Belgian salary tax rises in 1997 - minister.
newsitem.headline: No new Belgian salary tax rises in 1997 - minister.

text.p: Belgium's finance minister has promised there will be no surprise hike in deductions on salaries this year, even if other tax rises became necessary were the government unable to meet its 1997 budget target.
"There will be no new measures that increase deductions on revenue from work," Philippe Maystadt told Belgian RTL television in a pre-recorded discussion programme broadcast on Sunday.
"Moreover, the day it became possible we must do the reverse, because it's clear these deductions are too high in our country compared to those on other types of income," he added.

The 1997 budget, which includes an austerity package worth 80 billion Belgian francs ($2.5 billion), is due to be reviewed again this month to see whether it is still on track or whether further belt tightening is needed.
On Friday the Belgian government said it had failed to reach its self-set 1996 budget deficit target, but vowed to meet its 1997 goal of 2.9 percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP).
A three percent maximum is one of the Maastricht Treaty criteria for participation in a single European currency.

Belgium's 1996 deficit fell to 3.4 percent of GDP from 4.1 percent in 1995. The 1996 budget had been drawn up in 1995 with a deficit target of 3.0 percent of GDP, and in October 1996 - at the presentation of the 1997 budget - this target was revised upwards to 3.3 percent due to disappointing economic growth.
